title: Dzień w parku
note: A2 liść · the being-outdoors half of nature. a1_nature owns the big scenery and is never re-taught here: przyroda, pogoda, drzewo, kwiat, roślina, góra, wzgórze, rzeka, morze, jezioro, las, pole, wyspa, niebo, ziemia, powietrze, ogień. a1_animals owns ptak and owad, a1_city owns most, a2_travel owns mapa, plaża, góry, wycieczka and zwiedzać — all ANCHORS. This pack teaches 12 new words for what you actually meet on a walk (ścieżka, widok, liść, trawa, grzyby, staw, kamień, ławka, ognisko, plecak, wieś, świeży) plus five phrases that carry the inflected forms the sentences demand: na ścieżce, w trawie, na wsi, świeże powietrze, z plecakiem. Two badges worth flagging: grzyby takes pl (it is taught as the plural you pick and eat, so its past verb is były), and wieś takes f even though it ends in a consonant — the soft feminine family of noc and mysz. wieś → wsi is irregular enough to get its own explain. The payoff rides the past he now has (past_byc, past_ac, past_rest, past_plural) and one bedzie + infinitive sentence; the copular future (będę na wsi) is NOT used, because a2_bedzie fenced it. Split from a2_sport: this pack is landscape and being outdoors, a2_sport is games, exercise and watching. spacer and biegać went to a2_sport as exercise; plecak and ognisko stayed here as walking kit. Imperfective only, singular past except the one plural grzyby frame.

items.en: path (a track through a park or a wood)
view (what you can see from a spot)

sentences.en: The path in the park is nice.
sentences.explain: ścieżka ends in -a, so it is feminine, and the adjective has to follow it: ładna, not ładny.

sentences.en: Yesterday I was on the path. (m)
sentences.explain: Saying where you were puts the noun in the locative: ścieżka becomes ścieżce. It is the same swap you already make in praca → w pracy.

sentences.en: The view in the mountains was fantastic.
sentences.explain: widok is masculine, so the past być stays był and the adjective keeps its plain -y form.

sentences.en: I like this view.
sentences.explain: Lubię takes an object, but a masculine thing-word does not change at all: ten widok is both the subject form and the object form.

sentences.en: This leaf is green.
sentences.explain: liść ends in a soft consonant and is masculine — ten liść, and everything after it takes the masculine form.

sentences.en: In the morning the grass was cold.
sentences.explain: Feminine noun, so two -a endings follow it: była zimna. Exactly the pattern of kawa była dobra.

sentences.en: The dog was in the grass.
sentences.explain: w + locative again: trawa becomes trawie. The verb still agrees with pies, not with the grass.

sentences.en: There were mushrooms in the park.
sentences.explain: grzyby is a plural word, so the past być is były, not był — the same plural you use in wakacje były dobre.

sentences.en: Grandma liked mushrooms.
sentences.explain: The object of lubiła does not change here: plural thing-words keep the same form as subject and as object.

sentences.en: There is a pond in the park.
sentences.explain: This jest means "there is" — it announces that something exists in a place. It is not the to jest of naming something.

sentences.en: This stone is big.
The bench in the park is old.
In the evening there was a campfire.
sentences.explain: ognisko is neuter — that is why the past być is było, the same ending you already know from było dobrze.

sentences.en: I have a new rucksack.
sentences.explain: After mam a feminine word changes (mam kawę), but a masculine thing-word does not: mam nowy plecak.

sentences.en: Tomorrow I'm going to the park with a rucksack.
sentences.pl: Jutro idę do parku z plecakiem.
accepts: Jutro idę do parku z plecakiem.
Jutro idę do parku z plecakiem
Idę jutro do parku z plecakiem.
Idę jutro do parku z plecakiem
sentences.explain: z takes the instrumental, and masculine words add -em: plecak → plecakiem. Same ending as z bratem.

sentences.en: My grandma lived in the countryside.
sentences.explain: wieś loses its -e- in the locative: na wsi. It is worth learning as one piece — you will hear it far more often than the plain wieś.

sentences.en: This is an old village.
sentences.explain: wieś ends in a consonant but is feminine, like noc and mysz — so the adjective is stara, not stary.

sentences.en: Tomorrow I'll be relaxing in the countryside.
sentences.explain: będę plus the plain verb, and na wsi does not change — the future never touches the noun.

sentences.en: I like fresh air.
sentences.explain: powietrze is neuter, so the adjective takes -e: świeże. Neuter words also stay the same as an object, so nothing else moves.

sentences.en: In the mountains the air is fresh.
